findings.description: The gate's mode is now chosen solely by `.loa.config.yaml` `implement_gate.mode: authoritative`. In that mode the hook reads `tool_input.active_skill` to decide whether an App-Zone Write/Edit is inside /implement or /bug. The diff header itself states the PreToolUse payload carries no harness-set skill field and that `tool_input` is model-authored. So once an operator flips the flag, the fence is satisfiable by the model emitting `"active_skill": "implement"` inside its own Write tool_input, which defeats the C-PROC-001 fence the hook exists to enforce. The old code at least required `active_skill_available: true` from a detector; the new code offers a one-line config switch to a mode that is bypassable by construction, with no runtime warning that the trusted field is self-asserted.
findings.failure_mode: Operator enables authoritative mode expecting a stronger gate; the model (or a prompt-injected session) adds `active_skill` to Write/Edit tool_input and writes application code outside /implement without the fail-ask prompt, bypassing review and audit.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the authoritative mode until the platform actually supplies a harness-set skill indicator outside `tool_input`, or make the hook refuse authoritative mode (log and fall back to heuristic, exit non-zero on App-Zone writes) whenever `active_skill` is only present under `.tool_input`. At minimum emit a loud stderr warning on every invocation in authoritative mode and document in `.loa.config.yaml.example` that the field is model-authored.

findings.description: The evidence recorder is triggered by a model-authored field (`tool_input.active_skill`) and performs a read-modify-write of `.run/platform-features.json`. If the existing file is not a single parseable JSON object (corrupt, partial write from another writer, or multi-document), `_ig_base` is empty and the file is replaced with `{}` plus the three recorder keys, silently discarding whatever `detect-platform-features.sh` had recorded. The recorder also writes `active_skill_available: false` unconditionally, which can clobber a detector-set `true`. The write happens before the `file_path` empty check, so it runs for every Write/Edit hook invocation in a lead session.
findings.failure_mode: A model-emitted `active_skill` key causes the hook to rewrite shared platform-feature state, losing other detectors' keys; subsequent tools that consult `platform-features.json` see a degraded or default feature set.
findings.suggested_fix: Only merge when `jq -e 'type == "object"'` succeeds on the existing file (skip the write otherwise), do not set `active_skill_available` from the recorder (leave it to the detector), and move the recorder after the `file_path` guard so it runs only on real file-write events.

findings.description: The new grammar treats a trailing ` *` (space-star) the same as the documented `:*` prefix-wildcard, so `Bash(git push *)` is reported as covering the requirement `Bash(git push:*)` for both allow and deny. Claude Code's permission syntax documents `:*` as the prefix form; a rule body ending in ` *` is not guaranteed to be interpreted as a prefix match at runtime. If the runtime treats it as an exact string, the preflight checker reports an allow as present when the tool will actually prompt, and reports a deny as effective when the runtime will not deny it. The deny side is the security-relevant direction: the checker can tell an operator a dangerous command is blocked when it is not.
findings.failure_mode: Operator writes `Bash(rm *)` in permissions.deny, the checker reports the generic rm requirement as denied, but the runtime only denies the literal string and the command still runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept only the `:*` wildcard form that the runtime documents, or verify the ` *` behaviour against the Claude Code permission matcher and cite that in the header comment before treating it as equivalent. Add a bats case that pins whichever behaviour is confirmed.

findings.cross_file_justification: The help text in cheval.py and the comment in loa_cheval/providers/base.py document the FR-1.3 change; the cost-ceiling test in test_max_tokens_defaults.py only iterates Anthropic http_api entries, so the raised non-Anthropic default has no spend bound pinned.
findings.description: cycle-126 FR-1.3 raises the default output budget for every non-Anthropic provider from a fixed 4096 to min(16000, catalog max_output_tokens), a ~4x increase in worst-case output spend per call for OpenAI, Google, xAI and Bedrock hops. The only per-call cost-ceiling test (`test_worst_case_output_cost_per_call_is_bounded`) iterates Anthropic entries only, so the most expensive non-Anthropic entries (e.g. gpt-5.5-pro) have no pinned bound. Bounded dispatchers (flatline, dissent, BB) that relied on the historical 4096 to cap spend on cross-family panelists now pay up to 4x more per call without any config change.
findings.failure_mode: A runaway or repeated flatline/BB round on a high-priced non-Anthropic model emits up to 16K output tokens per call where it previously emitted 4K, quadrupling spend with no alert.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the cost-ceiling test to every http_api entry across providers and assert a per-call micro-USD bound, or pass an explicit `--max-tokens` from the bounded dispatchers (flatline-orchestrator, dissent, BB) so their budgets are not governed by the global default.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new `anthropic:claude-headless` row in .claude/data/model-permissions.yaml labels the hop `execution_mode: remote_model` with all capabilities false, while its own notes say `extra.allowed_tools` can widen what the local `claude -p` CLI does.
findings.description: The new Opus 5.5 entry terminates its fallback chain in `anthropic:claude-headless`, a `kind: cli` hop that spawns a local `claude -p` subprocess on the operator machine using the subscription account rather than the API key. An HTTP failure on the `opus` alias (now the default for jury panelists, flatline fallback and `LOA_OPUS_MODEL`) therefore silently moves the prompt, including any `security: redacted` context, onto a different auth principal and transport. The permissions registry models this hop as `remote_model` with no file or command capability, which is only true while the catalog's `extra.allowed_tools` stays empty; the trust row does not enforce that.
findings.failure_mode: API outage or ceiling rejection on Opus 5.5 degrades to the local CLI; if an operator has set `extra.allowed_tools` for another purpose, the review prompt runs with a tool loop the registry claims does not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the headless adapter refuse (or warn and strip) `extra.allowed_tools` when it is reached via fallback rather than selected explicitly, and add a test that the `claude-headless` catalog entry declares no `allowed_tools` so the `remote_model` registry row stays truthful.
